title: 📘 UNIT 9: THE AGE OF REVOLUTIONS, 1750s–1815
notes:
📅 Period: 1750s–1815

The period from the 1750s to 1815 was marked by major political, economic and social transformations in Europe, North America and other parts of the world.

title: 🏭 9.1 INDUSTRIAL CAPITALISM IN EUROPE
notes:
The Industrial Revolution began in Great Britain during the late 18th century and later spread to other parts of Europe, North America and other regions.

⚙️ Industrial Revolution → the transition from mainly handmade production to machine-based manufacturing.

🏠 Before industrialization:
• Farming was the dominant activity.
• Most goods were produced by hand.
• Production often took place in homes and small workshops.

🏭 After industrialization:
• Machines became central to production.
• Factories replaced much home production.
• Manufacturing became large-scale.
• Production of cloth, iron and steel increased greatly.

⛏️ Britain had important supplies of coal and iron, which supported industrial development.

title: 💰 Industrial Capitalism
notes:
🏦 Industrial capitalism → an economic system based on the large accumulation of capital used to finance the production of commodities.

📌 Main characteristics:
• Accumulation of capital
• Private property
• Protection of property rights
• Competitive markets
• Price system
• Voluntary exchange
• Wage labour

⚙️ Technological development became an important force behind industrial capitalism.

🚂 Steam technology led to the development of locomotives and railways.

🚆 Railways:
• Reduced transportation costs
• Opened new markets
• Made movement of raw materials easier
• Connected industrial regions with wider markets

title: 🛒 CAPITALISM & FREE-MARKET ECONOMY
notes:
The development of industrial capitalism challenged the older mercantilist system, which relied on trade barriers, protective restrictions and monopolies.

📈 The growth of capitalism encouraged:
• Free-market economic activity
• Greater competition
• Liberal economic ideas
• Reduced mercantilist restrictions

🇬🇧 Britain became known as the “world's workshop” during the 19th century because of its industrial strength and manufacturing output.

💡 New technologies also transformed business and communication.

📞 Examples included:
• Telephone
• Typewriter
• Electricity

These technologies improved communication, record-keeping and the organization of business activities.

title: 🏭 9.1.1 POLITICAL, ECONOMIC & SOCIAL EFFECTS OF INDUSTRIAL REVOLUTION
notes:
Industrialization produced major political, economic and social changes.

🏛️ Political effects:
• Industrial interests gained greater political influence.
• Political structures changed.
• Workers organized protests and strikes.
• Labour became an important political issue.

💰 Economic effects:
• Agriculture and handicrafts became less dominant.
• Mechanized manufacturing expanded.
• Factories became central to production.
• Production of goods increased.
• Industrial wealth expanded.
• Many goods became cheaper.
• Living standards improved for some sections of society.
• Housing, education and diets improved in many areas.

🏙️ Social effects:
• Rapid urbanization occurred.
• New social classes developed.
• Industrial society became increasingly divided between owners and wage labourers.

title: 👥 BOURGEOISIE & PROLETARIAT
notes:
Industrialization created new social classes with different economic positions.

💼 Bourgeoisie → people who owned factories, machines, raw materials and finished products.

👷 Proletariat → wage labourers who depended mainly on selling their labour for income.

📌 Problems faced by workers included:
• Low wages
• Strict factory discipline
• Unemployment
• Long and difficult working conditions
• Child labour

👶 Children were employed in many factories and worked under harsh conditions.

⚠️ Industrialization also produced serious social and environmental problems, including pollution, poor sanitation, diseases and unsafe workplaces.

title: 🚂 Railways & Industrial Society
notes:
Railways became one of the most important developments of industrialization.

🚆 Railways:
• Connected different regions
• Reduced transportation costs
• Allowed raw materials to reach factories
• Helped manufactured goods reach markets
• Encouraged national economic integration
• Increased political and cultural connections

🌍 Industrialization therefore transformed not only production but also transportation, communication, urban life and relationships between different regions.

title: 🇫🇷 9.2 FRENCH REVOLUTION
notes:
📅 French Revolution → 1787–1799

The French Revolution was one of the most important political revolutions of the modern era.

🔥 Major outbreak → July 14, 1789
🏰 Event → Storming of the Bastille

The revolution challenged the old system of feudal privileges and absolute monarchy.

📅 1799 → The revolutionary period ended when Napoleon Bonaparte overthrew the revolutionary government and established his political authority.

📌 The revolution introduced powerful ideas of:
• Liberty
• Equality
• Popular sovereignty
• Constitutional government
• Nationalism

title: ⚠️ Causes of the French Revolution
notes:
The French Revolution resulted from a combination of political, social, economic and intellectual problems.

🏛️ Political causes:
• Absolute monarchy
• Inefficient government
• Weak leadership
• Financial bankruptcy

👥 Social causes:
• Feudal oppression
• Unequal privileges
• Division of society into privileged and non-privileged groups
• Heavy burden on the Third Estate

💡 Intellectual causes:
• Enlightenment ideas
• Criticism of absolute monarchy
• Opposition to feudal privileges
• Ideas of liberty and equality

🌍 External influences:
• English Bourgeois Revolution
• American War of Independence

💰 Economic difficulties:
• High taxation
• Poverty
• Rising prices
• Increasing price of bread and other necessities

title: 👑 FRENCH SOCIETY: THE THREE ESTATES
notes:
French society before the revolution was divided into three Estates.

1️⃣ First Estate → Clergy and royal family
• Owned large amounts of land
• Enjoyed important privileges
• Generally exempt from taxation

2️⃣ Second Estate → Nobility
• Owned extensive land
• Had political, social and economic privileges
• Generally exempt from taxation

3️⃣ Third Estate → Peasants and bourgeoisie
• Largest section of society
• Had few privileges
• Many peasants owned little or no land
• Paid heavy taxes
• Experienced exploitation

⚠️ The unequal distribution of privileges and taxation created strong resentment and revolutionary tension.

title: 🏛️ ESTATES-GENERAL & BEGINNING OF THE REVOLUTION
notes:
📅 May 5, 1789 → King Louis XVI called the Estates-General because France faced severe financial problems and bankruptcy.

⚖️ Conflict developed between the privileged Estates and the Third Estate.

📅 June 17, 1789 → The Third Estate declared itself the National Assembly.

🔥 July 14, 1789 → The Bastille was stormed by revolutionaries.

This event became a major symbol of the revolution and demonstrated that Louis XVI was losing effective control.

🏃 June 1791 → Louis XVI attempted to escape France but was captured at Varennes.

📜 September 1791 → A constitution established a limited monarchy.

title: 📜 NATIONAL ASSEMBLY REFORMS, 1789–1791
notes:
The National Assembly introduced major political and social reforms that weakened the old feudal and absolutist order.

🔥 August Days → Feudal privileges were abolished.

📜 Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen:
• Promoted liberty
• Promoted equality
• Asserted political rights
• Challenged traditional privileges

📜 Constitution of 1791:
• Established a limited monarchy
• Created constitutional government
• Introduced political participation based on citizenship

🗳️ Active citizens → men who met the required tax qualification and could vote.

👥 Passive citizens → citizens who did not meet the voting qualification.

⛪ Church reforms:
• Church lands were confiscated.
• Monasteries were suppressed.

These reforms weakened feudalism, absolutism and the traditional political power of the Church.

title: ⚔️ FRENCH REPUBLIC & WAR
notes:
Political divisions developed between moderate and radical revolutionaries.

🌍 Austria and Prussia supported the French monarchy and opposed the revolution.

📅 April 1792 → France declared war.

⚔️ September 20, 1792 → French forces won the Battle of Valmy.

🏛️ September 22, 1792 → France was proclaimed a republic.

👑 Louis XVI was tried for treason.

📅 December 1792 → Trial began.
📅 January 21, 1793 → Louis XVI was executed.

🎵 La Marseillaise became the national anthem of revolutionary France.

The establishment of the republic marked the destruction of the French monarchy and intensified the revolutionary struggle.

title: ⚔️ GIRONDISTS & JACOBINS
notes:
Two important political groups competed for control of revolutionary France.

🟦 Girondists:
• Represented mainly the big and middle bourgeoisie
• Generally associated with the right wing of the revolutionary movement
• Favoured a more moderate approach

🟥 Jacobins:
• Represented the revolutionary left
• Became dominant in 1793
• Supported strong revolutionary government

📅 June 1793 → Jacobins defeated the Girondists.

📜 June 24, 1793 → A new constitution was adopted.

⚔️ Reign of Terror → a period of revolutionary dictatorship and campaigns against counter-revolutionaries and other perceived enemies of the revolution.

👤 Robespierre became the leading figure of the Jacobin government.

⚔️ Guillotine → the famous instrument used for executions during the Terror.

📅 July 1794 → Robespierre and his followers were executed, bringing the Jacobin dictatorship to an end.

title: 🌍 CONSEQUENCES OF THE FRENCH REVOLUTION
notes:
The French Revolution had major political, social and economic consequences in France and beyond.

🏛️ Political and social changes:
• Destroyed much of the old feudal order
• Reduced traditional privileges
• Promoted liberty and equality
• Strengthened the bourgeoisie
• Reduced the political importance of religion

💰 Economic effects:
• Encouraged capitalism
• Helped create conditions for industrial capitalism
• Weakened feudal economic structures

🌍 Wider influence:
• Spread ideas of nationalism and liberalism
• Inspired later revolutionary movements
• Influenced political developments outside France
• Became a major source of modern political ideas

⚠️ Limitations:
• Rights were not extended equally to everyone.
• Conditions of working people did not fundamentally improve.
• Political leadership increasingly passed to the bourgeoisie.

title: 🇫🇷 9.3 NAPOLEONIC ERA
notes:
📅 Napoleonic Era → 1799–1815

👤 Napoleon Bonaparte was a French military and political leader who rose to power after the French Revolution.

📅 1799 → Napoleon seized power through a coup and became First Consul.

📅 1802 → Became Consul for Life.

📅 December 2, 1804 → Crowned Emperor of France.

🏛️ His government became a centralized military dictatorship.

Napoleon combined revolutionary reforms with strong personal political control and used military power to expand French influence across Europe.

title: 📜 NAPOLEON'S LEGAL & ADMINISTRATIVE REFORMS
notes:
⚖️ Napoleonic Code, 1804:
• Established uniform civil laws
• Promoted civil equality regardless of birth, wealth or rank
• Strengthened the rule of law

🏛️ Administrative reforms:
• Centralized government
• Strengthened state administration
• Introduced merit-based government employment and promotion
• Improved revenue collection

These reforms weakened many traditional privileges and helped spread legal and administrative principles associated with the revolution.

title: 🏦 NAPOLEON'S ECONOMIC, RELIGIOUS & EDUCATIONAL REFORMS
notes:
💰 Economic reforms:
• National Bank of France established in 1800
• Public works were expanded
• Roads and bridges were constructed
• Major public buildings, monuments and palaces were developed

⛪ Religious reforms:
📅 1801 → Agreement with the Roman Catholic Church.
• The Church accepted the loss of confiscated lands.
• The government paid clergy.
• Relations between the state and Church were reorganized.

🎓 Educational reforms:
• Expanded education
• Established state secondary schools
• Strengthened universities

⚠️ Political limitations:
• Dictatorial government
• Press censorship
• Strong police and army
• Restricted democracy

title: 🗺️ NAPOLEON'S EUROPEAN EMPIRE
notes:
By 1808, Napoleon controlled or influenced a large part of Europe.

📍 His empire and areas under French control included:
• France
• Belgium
• Spain
• Holland
• Switzerland
• Italy
• Southern and western German states
• Poland

🤝 At different times, Russia, Prussia, Denmark and Norway were also allies or associated with Napoleon.

📜 Revolutionary principles spread through French control:
• Civil equality
• Liberty
• Individualism
• Secularism
• Religious toleration
• Abolition of serfdom
• Rule of law

⚠️ However, French occupation also brought:
• Heavy taxation
• Economic exploitation
• Political control

These policies encouraged nationalist resistance against French rule.

title: ⚔️ FALL OF NAPOLEON
notes:
🇬🇧 Britain remained a major opponent of Napoleon.

⚓ 1805 → Battle of Trafalgar
• Admiral Nelson defeated the combined French and Spanish naval forces.
• French hopes of controlling the seas were weakened.

🛒 Continental System → Napoleon attempted to weaken Britain by restricting European trade with Britain, but the policy failed.

🇪🇸 Spain, 1808–1812:
• Spanish nationalist resistance developed.
• British forces supported the resistance.

🇷🇺 Russia, 1812:
• Napoleon invaded Russia.
• Russian forces withdrew strategically.
• Scorched-earth tactics denied supplies to the French army.
• Hunger, cold and disease destroyed much of Napoleon's army.

⚔️ 1813 → Napoleon was defeated at Leipzig by a coalition of European powers.

📅 March 31, 1814 → Coalition forces occupied Paris.

📅 1814 → Napoleon abdicated and was exiled to Elba.

title: 🏝️ HUNDRED DAYS & WATERLOO
notes:
📅 March 20, 1815 → Napoleon returned from Elba and regained power.

⏳ This period became known as the Hundred Days.

⚔️ June 18, 1815 → Battle of Waterloo

Napoleon was defeated by forces led by the Duke of Wellington and supported by Prussian forces.

🏝️ After Waterloo:
• Napoleon was permanently removed from power.
• He was exiled to the island of Saint Helena.

📅 1821 → Napoleon died.

📌 His rule had spread revolutionary legal and administrative ideas across Europe while also stimulating nationalist resistance to French domination.

title: 🇺🇸 9.4 AMERICAN WAR OF INDEPENDENCE
notes:
📅 American War of Independence → 1775–1783

The thirteen British colonies in North America fought against British rule and eventually became an independent nation.

🇺🇸 Result → Emergence of the United States of America.

🏘️ The colonies had been established mainly by British settlers between 1607 and 1682.

⚔️ Conflict developed as the colonies increasingly opposed British political and economic control.

📌 The struggle became an important example of colonial resistance, independence and constitutional government.

title: 🔥 CAUSES & BEGINNING OF AMERICAN INDEPENDENCE
notes:
💰 Main cause → British taxation of the thirteen colonies.

The colonists strongly opposed heavy taxation and British economic control.

🏛️ First Continental Congress → met in Philadelphia.

📌 Actions included:
• Non-importation agreements
• Non-consumption agreements
• Organized colonial resistance

📅 May 10, 1775 → Congress established the Army of the United Colonies.

👤 Commander → George Washington

⚔️ Fighting began in major cities and trading ports.

📅 1776 → Representatives declared independence.

📜 Declaration of Independence → drafted mainly by Thomas Jefferson.

🇺🇸 The Declaration marked the political birth of the United States and expressed ideas about human freedom that influenced later movements.

title: 📜 AMERICAN CONSTITUTION
notes:
📅 September 17, 1787 → The United States Constitution was adopted.

🏛️ Main principles:
• Limited government
• Constitutional government
• Separation of powers
• Three branches of government
• Constitution as the supreme law
• Peaceful transfer of political power

🏛️ Three branches:
1️⃣ Legislative → makes laws
2️⃣ Executive → carries out laws
3️⃣ Judicial → interprets laws

⚖️ Federalists and Anti-Federalists disagreed over the Constitution, but it was eventually ratified.

🇺🇸 George Washington became the first President of the United States.

title: 🌎 CONSEQUENCES OF THE AMERICAN WAR OF INDEPENDENCE
notes:
🇺🇸 Major consequences:
• Thirteen colonies became independent.
• The United States of America was established.
• An independent government was created.
• Constitutional government developed.
• The revolution influenced the French Revolution.
• It encouraged later Latin American independence movements.
• It supported the development of capitalist economic activity.

⚠️ Limitations:
• Slavery was not abolished.
• Native Americans were not recognized as citizens.

📌 Legacy → The American Revolution became an important example for later democratic, constitutional and nationalist movements.

title: 🏛️ 9.5 CONGRESS OF VIENNA
notes:
📅 Congress of Vienna → 1814–1815

The Congress began in September 1814 and its Final Act was signed on June 9, 1815.

🎯 Main purpose → Establish long-term peace in Europe after the French Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars.

🌍 Almost every European state was represented.

⭐ Four major powers:
• Austria
• Prussia
• Russia
• Great Britain

📌 Main objectives:
• Reorganize Europe
• Restore political stability
• Prevent another dominant European power
• Establish a balance of power

title: 🗺️ MAJOR ISSUES & SETTLEMENTS OF VIENNA
notes:
The Congress faced disagreements over territories and political arrangements in:
• Poland
• Saxony
• Sweden
• Denmark
• Russia
• German states
• Italian territories

📌 Major settlements:
• Poland came largely under Russian influence.
• German states were organized into a loose confederation.
• Austria gained Lombardy and Venice.
• The Kingdom of the Netherlands was strengthened as a barrier against France.
• Italian territories were reorganized, with strong Austrian influence.
• Switzerland received a new constitutional arrangement.
• International rivers were opened for free navigation.
• Rules concerning diplomatic precedence were established.

title: ⚖️ BALANCE OF POWER
notes:
⚖️ Balance of power → an arrangement designed to prevent any single European state from becoming overwhelmingly powerful.

📅 June 9, 1815 → Final Act of the Congress of Vienna was signed.

📌 Major outcomes:
• European boundaries were reorganized.
• The balance-of-power principle was strengthened.
• Territorial changes shaped European politics for decades.
• Europe experienced a relatively long period of peace.

⚠️ Limitations:
• National aspirations were often ignored.
• Territories were transferred without considering the wishes of their inhabitants.
• No permanent institution was created that could fully adapt to the political forces of the 19th century.

📌 The settlement helped preserve peace but could not prevent the later growth of nationalism and future conflicts.

title: 🔗 CONNECTION BETWEEN THE REVOLUTIONS
notes:
The major revolutions and political developments of the period were closely connected.

🏭 Industrial Revolution → growth of industrial capitalism.

🇺🇸 American Revolution → creation of the United States and development of capitalist and constitutional government.

💡 Enlightenment ideas → encouraged revolutionary thinking in France and America.

🇺🇸 American Revolution → influenced the French Revolution.

🇫🇷 French Revolution →
• Destroyed feudal privileges
• Promoted liberty and equality
• Encouraged nationalism and liberalism

🇫🇷 Napoleon → spread revolutionary legal and political ideas throughout Europe.

⚔️ Napoleon's conquests → encouraged nationalist resistance.

🏛️ Congress of Vienna → attempted to restore European stability and maintain a balance of power after the revolutionary and Napoleonic wars.
